title: Optimal exact single-source shortest paths in CONGEST
formal: For every fixed integer b≥1, do there exist constants K,c>0 and a uniform randomized CONGEST algorithm which, on every connected simple undirected graph with n≥2 vertices, integer edge weights in [0,n^b] and a designated source s, makes every vertex output its exact weighted distance from s in at most K(√n+D)(log₂(n+2))^c rounds on every execution, with simultaneous correctness probability at least 1−n^(−3)? Here D is the diameter of the unweighted graph.

definitions: A path length is the sum of its edge weights; the distance is the minimum path length, and the source distance is zero. D is the maximum over vertex pairs of the minimum number of edges on a path between them. The graph itself is the network. In each synchronous round, each endpoint of each edge can send at most B⌈log₂(n+2)⌉ bits to the other endpoint, for a constant B depending only on b. Nodes initially know n,b, the source identifier, their own identifiers, and the identifiers and weights of incident neighbours. Identifiers are distinct integers in [n²]. Local computation and memory are unrestricted, but each local computation between rounds terminates. Nodes use independent private fair random bits. One finite program, allowed to depend on b, runs at all nodes; no global graph description, advice, routing tables or preprocessing is supplied. The graph, weights, source and identifiers are fixed before randomness is drawn. Output at v is an ordinary binary integer for dist(s,v), stored locally. The guarantee concerns all vertices together, over all coins. All communication, including finding termination and any preprocessing, counts in the round bound. K,c,B are independent of n,D and the instance; no value of D is initially supplied.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.

sentences: Single-source shortest paths asks every vertex to learn its exact distance from one source in a weighted network.
In CONGEST, each edge carries only a logarithmic number of bits per communication round.
The target is a randomized algorithm using roughly sqrt(n) plus the hop diameter D rounds, ignoring polylogarithmic factors.
The graph is undirected and connected, with nonnegative polynomially bounded integer edge weights.
Achieving this bound would combine global distance propagation with the bandwidth limits of the network at the scale identified by the saved problem statement.
